description:
fz-gk4 made the second slot of `#fn<a/b>` the closure's arity (Elixir's `#Function<index.uniq/arity>` reports arity there). The FIRST slot is still `closure_schema_id` — the id of the interned `ClosureEnv{n}` schema, assigned in allocation order and keyed purely by capture count.

Consequences:
- Two closures with the same capture count share a rendered identity, so identity does not distinguish.
- interp and native render different leading ids for the same program: fixtures2/behavior/enum_reduce_suspend and closure_render_arity each need a separate .expected.interp.txt golden solely for this.
- Any change to allocation order shifts the id, so goldens that print a closure stay fragile in the one remaining slot.

Elixir's leading component is `new_index.uniq`: the fun's source-order index within its module plus a hash of the module's code — source-derived, stable across runs and lanes (../elixir/lib/elixir/lib/inspect.ex:589).

Direction: make the env schema per closure SITE rather than per capture count. `Heap::alloc_closure_slots_with_schema` already takes a verbatim schema id, and a per-site schema is what a closure environment actually is (named capture fields), so this REMOVES the capture-count bucket rather than adding a concept. The callable-boundary id is the natural source-order key and is already in hand at every construction site.

Research first: `alloc_closure_slots_with_schema`'s doc comment warns that registering per-site schemas perturbs the schema-id space the AOT runtime must keep byte-identical to compile time. Size that before committing.

Acceptance: the leading slot derives from the closure's source identity; interp and native agree on it; enum_reduce_suspend and closure_render_arity each drop to a single golden.
title: Rendered closure identity is an allocation-order env-schema id, not a source-derived fun index
